coverageAssessment.evidence: Unit and component tests cover the seven fields and stable decision ID.
coverageAssessment.gap: The inventory does not demonstrate that the ID remains unchanged across an actual component re-render.

coverageAssessment.evidence: Component test verifies meaningful accessible names and fixture source order.
Component tests cover keyboard and pointer activation and verify focus alone causes no state change.
Tests cover empty, overlong, absent, malformed, past, and valid deferral inputs.
Reload tests use the injected adapter and cover successful persistence, corruption, and adapter-load failure.
Core tests cover duplicate, stale, malformed, and out-of-order events with named refusals and exact state preservation.
Core tests verify distinct non-colour signatures for all seven statuses; component tests cover rendered saving and unavailable states.
Tests use injected clocks and verify source cannot reach ambient time, randomness, timers, storage, or network.
coverageAssessment.gap: The described evidence does not establish byte-identical output across runs or verify an injected ID source independently.

coverageAssessment.evidence: Browser evidence records 200% zoom, reduced motion, reflow, no overflow, and accessibility results.
coverageAssessment.gap: Evidence does not establish that every inventory state preserves its name and structure under both conditions at both approved viewports.

coverageAssessment.evidence: Component tests cover focus restoration after validation, success, failure, reload, undo, and retry.
Source scanning, isolation journeys, request logs, credential scans, and storage-write scans exist.
coverageAssessment.gap: The evidence does not explicitly prove absence of destructive, deployment, or paid side effects beyond the tested journeys.

coverageAssessment.evidence: Core tests cover both second-action directions and reject mutually exclusive actions.
Tests cover undo after acknowledgement and deferral, separate undo events, and retained history.
Tests cover all three severities and an explicitly named unknown severity.
Tests cover ISO-8601 UTC storage, locale-dependent rendering, malformed dates, and persisted review dates.
Core tests cover resolved, missing, invalid, and unavailable links; isolation evidence records fixture-only resolution and zero external requests.
No screen-reader walkthrough record exists; the criterion is explicitly waived.
coverageAssessment.gap: A recorded human walkthrough naming screen reader, build, exercised paths, and omissions is missing.

coverageAssessment.evidence: The provenance ledger records 284 artifacts, digests, producers, and supersession enforcement; unknown producers are explicitly recorded rather than guessed.
There are 40 captures, accessibility trees, fidelity checks, and an owner whole-inventory acceptance.
coverageAssessment.gap: The owner acceptance has no per-state marks, and the visual reviewer did not see the images; browser evidence is only Chromium.

coverageAssessment.evidence: The defined nine-journey isolation procedure records console, network, credential, storage, and evidence-resolution results, including a deliberately caught external-fetch failure.
No independent promoted release-review verdict is provided.
coverageAssessment.gap: A release-reviewer-authored needs-work or eligible-for-owner-approval verdict citing artifact and evidence versions is missing.

missingNegativePaths: Actual component re-render with an attempted decision-ID mutation.
Two-run byte comparison using independently injected ID sources and fixtures.
Every rendered inventory state under reduced motion and 200% zoom at both approved viewports.
Pointer and keyboard attempts against every disabled control.
Browser journeys for missing, invalid, and unavailable evidence links.
Explicit attempts to trigger deployment, destructive, paid, or credential side effects.
A complete supersession-chain negative case showing a current artifact citing a superseded artifact.
A second browser implementation or an explicit approved-browser-matrix exception.
Human screen-reader traversal of the complete actionable surface.

steps: Run each defined journey: acknowledge-then-undo, defer-then-undo, empty-reason refusal, overlong-reason refusal, past-date refusal, save failure, resolved evidence inspection, overdue read-only, and disabled refusal.
Record the complete request and console logs for each journey.
Scan rendered document, console, and persisted state for credential-shaped strings.
Record every storage write target, including localStorage, sessionStorage, and indexedDB.
Verify every evidence resolution is limited to supplied fixture artifacts.
Inject a deliberate external fetch and verify the detector records it as a failure.
isolationProcedure.passCondition: Every journey completes with zero external requests, zero credential-shaped output, zero writes outside the injected fixture, and evidence resolution limited to fixture artifacts.
isolationProcedure.failureEvidence: A deliberate violation must produce deterministic recorded failure evidence identifying the violating request, output, write, or resolution, rather than merely making the run fail silently.

required: C-01/C-02: accessibility trees showing all fields, stable ID, meaningful ordered links.
C-03/C-04/C-10/C-12/C-13: keyboard and pointer journeys, focus destinations, validation refusals, successful actions, mutual exclusion, and undo.
C-07/C-14/C-15/C-16: captures and accessibility trees for every status, severity, date, and evidence outcome.
C-09: every inventory state at both approved viewports under reduced motion and 200% zoom, with overflow and structure checks.
C-11/C-20: complete console, network, credential-scan, storage-write, and fixture-resolution records.
C-19: per-state owner fidelity decisions tied to current-build captures at both viewports.
deterministicBrowserEvidence.blockedBy: C-17 lacks the required human walkthrough; C-19 lacks per-state owner marks and image-seeing visual review; only Chromium evidence is present; and the described evidence does not prove every state under both zoom and reduced-motion conditions.

C-17 is waived and has no screen-reader evidence.
C-19 lacks per-state owner fidelity marks and image-based visual review.
No non-Chromium browser evidence is present.
